title: test-0048-SCI-CHM-CHANGES
passage: In our science lab today, we performed three experiments to distinguish between physical and chemical changes. First, we placed a clean iron nail in a beaker of water and left it exposed to air for a week. We observed a reddish-brown deposit forming on the surface, which is a new substance called iron oxide, formed by the reaction of iron with oxygen and moisture. Second, we dissolved a spoonful of sugar into a glass of water. Although the sugar seemed to disappear, we could recover it by evaporating the water, proving that no new substance was created. Third, we took a piece of paper and tore it into small fragments. While the shape and size of the paper changed, the material remained paper, confirming it was a physical change. Finally, we discussed how stainless steel is an alloy that resists corrosion due to its internal composition, not because of any external paint. We learned that chemical changes involve the formation of new substances with different properties, whereas physical changes only alter the physical state or appearance of matter without changing its identity. It is important to remember that not all changes involving bubbles or color shifts are chemical; sometimes, they are just physical processes like boiling or simple mixing.
summary: In our science lab today, we did three experiments to tell if something is physical or chemical. We learned that chemical changes make new substances with different properties, while physical changes just change the state or look of matter without changing its identity.
